sense.text: “Measure thou the time diligently in itself: and when thou seest part of the signs past, which I have told thee before, Then shalt thou understand, that it is the very same time, wherein the Highest will begin to visit the world which he made.” The Most High is going to visit this world, and we are seeing the signs of it now. All them fires up there in California: I see what’s happening. So for you to fall out of this truth, you very foolish.

“Therefore when there shall be seen earthquakes”: didn’t we just read about that in Isaiah? “And uproars of the people”: the uproars of the people are that damn Antifa group and all these other groups running around, mad because of Covid and all this other stuff. That’s uproars of the people. Even the thing with our sister Breonna Taylor, our people, is the uproars of the people: how could Daniel Cameron do what he did.

Listen, these things are going to happen, they’re going to keep happening. We can’t get caught up into it though.

“The most High spake of those things from the days that were before thee, even from the beginning.” “Even so the times also of the Highest have plain beginnings in wonder and powerful works, and endings in effects and signs”: the same way, the Most High is going to have powerful effects in these last days.

“And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith”: by his works and by faith. Those are the ones that “shall be preserved from the said perils, and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders: for I have sanctified them for me from the beginning.”

“Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments.” Who casts God’s words away? The wicked. They cast God’s words behind them.

“For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me”: for such meaning what? You have people amongst us, Israelite people, Israel, Blacks and Latinos, who follow the example of so-called white people.

Put Creflo up first: we’re going to look at the benefits, and have not known him. The hell is this now? This guy is crazy. Then my buddy. Well, alrighty then. These are benefits, like the scripture said: “For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me”.

“And they that have loathed my law”: all these ministers have that in common. The benefits they receive are a result of them loathing, hating, God’s law. “While they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it”: that’s how you know it’s speaking of somebody of Israel. The place of repentance was open unto them, and they despised it.
“The same must know it after death by pain.” You ain’t going to get away; nobody gets away. That means there is pain after death: not for us, but for them. Revelation 14 explains it.

“Be thou not curious how the ungodly shall be punished, and when: but enquire how the righteous shall be saved, whose the world is, and for whom the world is created.” The world belongs to the righteous; the world is created for the righteous. That’s Israel.

Ezra says “there be many more of them which perish, than of them which shall be saved: Like as a wave is greater than a drop.” And he is answered, “Like as the field is, so is also the seed”, “and as the husbandman is himself, so is his husbandry also”. Husbandry means planting; a husbandman is someone that takes care of crops.

“And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” That verse is funny when you look at the Christian commentaries. Google that verse and it says no man spake against God because they did not exist yet. But look at verse 19: “For then every one obeyed.” What do you mean they didn’t exist, you dumb stupid Christians?

In the spiritual world all of us were there, every last man, woman, boy and girl, everybody on the planet. He said, this group over here, you’re going to play Moab; this group over there, you’re going to play Israel; you’re going to play Ham; you’re going to be Esau; you’re going to be Ammon. Everybody said, yes Lord. Now he set us on the planet, and everybody want to rebel and run their damn mouth. That’s what it means.

“For then every one obeyed: but now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”: that sin seed that Esau got in him. “And by a law which is unsearchable rid themselves”: they want to get rid of God’s laws.
“So I considered the world, and, behold, there was peril because of the devices that were come into it”: the devices that came into it are sin.

“And have kept me a grape of the cluster”: that’s the elect of the Israelites, the elect of God, “and a plant of a great people.”

“Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”: that’s some heavy stuff right there. Imagine telling people that. Let the multitude perish means let the multitude die. “And let my grape be kept, and my plant”: that’s Israel, “for with great labour have I made it perfect.”

precepts.why: This is the Highest visiting the world: “Thou shalt be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire.” All them fires up there in California: that is the flame of devouring fire. We see what’s happening, and the earthquakes of 2 Esdras 9:3 are the same earthquakes we just read here. For you to fall out of this truth, you very foolish.

Saved and able to escape “by his works, and by faith”: Revelation gives the same two things. “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” Keeping the commandments of God is the works; the faith of Jesus is the faith. Now we understand who shall be preserved and see the Most High’s salvation in his land.

Who casts God’s words away? “Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” That’s talking about the wicked: they cast God’s words behind them. These are the ones that “have cast them away despitefully” and “shall dwell in torments.”

This is what “The same must know it after death by pain” means: there is pain after we die, not for us but for them. “If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead”: that’s worshipping the white image of Jesus and following his political policies. “Or in his hand”: sum it up in one word, sin.

“The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone”: this is that lake of fire, “in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever”.

“And they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.” So don’t think just because your body is burnt up that it’s over: your spirit is still going to get tormented. That’s what Revelation is saying. Now we know what 2 Esdras 9:12 is talking about.

No man spake against God when he prepared the world, because everyone was already there in the spirit. “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” Jeremiah was chosen to be a prophet in the spiritual realm before he was ever born. So it was with all of us: in the spiritual world every man, woman, boy and girl was there, and each was given the part to play, Israel, Moab, Ham, Esau, Ammon, and everybody obeyed.

sense.text: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” And he answers, “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.” Ezra is going back to the history according to Genesis 25.

Now he’s telling you what it signified when Jacob held first to the heel of Esau: “For Esau is the end of the world”. Esau would be the last Gentile nation ruling. “And Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth”: the Israelites would be the next ruling kingdom.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: the hand of man is all the other nations. “Other question, Esdras, ask thou not.” This whole thing on planet earth is between Jacob and Esau. It’s like when you got stars and co-stars: Moab, Ammon and all the other nations are like extras. They don’t mean a hill of beans; they’re just there. This whole thing deals with Jacob and Esau, and that’s it.

“And when the world, that shall begin to vanish away, shall be finished, then will I shew these tokens: the books shall be opened before the firmament, and they shall see all together”: this is talking about the judgment seat of Christ, when you read Corinthians.

“And when the world, that shall begin to vanish away”: that’s Esau’s world going to vanish away, “shall be finished, then will I shew these tokens”: this is Jacob’s time to rule. Israel is going to rule now.

“And the children of a year old shall speak with their voices, the women with child shall bring forth untimely children of three or four months old, and they shall live, and be raised up.” This is going into the kingdom right now. Remember, every generation we grow weaker and smaller, but in the kingdom it’s going to be reversed. We’re going to be on God level.

In the kingdom, when the child is one, it’s going to be talking. And the women ain’t got to wait nine months: God says in three or four months children are going to be born. This is how he’s going to speed this thing up. And these children are going to grow up fast; it ain’t going to be, we got to wait twenty years for them to grow. This is going to be on a righteous level, on God level. That’s why Corinthians says we shall all be changed.

“And they shall live, and be raised up”: the children are going to grow quick. There’s going to be no waiting twenty years before they become a man; they’re going to be raised up quick.

“And suddenly shall the sown places appear unsown, the full storehouses shall suddenly be found empty”: that’s this place down here, talking about America. We think this world is all there is, but the Lord said this thing y’all living in is garbage, it’s nothing, and he is going to wipe it away.
“And the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man heareth, they shall be suddenly afraid.” That trumpet is the trump of God that Paul writes about.

“At that time shall friends fight one against another like enemies”: that’s nation against nation. “The springs of the fountains shall stand still, and in three hours they shall not run”: the oceans are going to stop. There ain’t going to be no raging water; the water is going to be still on that day.

“Whosoever remaineth from all these that I have told thee shall escape, and see my salvation, and the end of your world.” The end of your world is the end of Esau’s world. Go back to verse 9: “For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” That’s what it means.

“And the men that are received shall see it, who have not tasted death from their birth”: that’s the group of men that is going to be alive when the Lord returns, what Paul was talking about. “And the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning”: that’s what we read in Corinthians. Celestial bodies, God bodies.

“For evil shall be put out, and deceit shall be quenched. As for faith, it shall flourish, corruption shall be overcome, and the truth, which hath been so long without fruit, shall be declared.”

What does it mean, the truth had no fruit? You know how many times we tell Esau and the nations they’re going into slavery, and they go, yeah, yeah, yeah. The truth is without fruit. But on this day we’re reading about, when them chains are put on them, shackles on their necks and their arms and their feet, we’re going to declare this truth and we’re going to rejoice.

precepts.why: “The books shall be opened before the firmament, and they shall see all together”: pay attention. “But why dost thou judge thy brother? or why dost thou set at nought thy brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.” We shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ. This is about the kingdom: when we get in the wilderness, he’s going to deal with us face to face. That’s the judgment seat.

The kingdom is coming, y’all. “Thy people also shall be all righteous”: guess what, brothers, them women over there, all the women are going to be righteous. Are they righteous right now? Oh hell no. Remember the Bible says all our righteousness is as filthy rags; we wicked as hell, we trying. But in the kingdom everybody is going to be righteous, men and women.

“They shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified. A little one shall become a thousand”: one brother shall become a thousand, he going to have a thousand children, “and a small one a strong nation”. How is this possible? 2 Esdras 6:21 shows how: the children of a year old speaking and the women bringing forth at three or four months.

Men, pay attention; I’m dealing with the women right now. “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow”: this is going into her menstrual cycle and her labour pains. “And thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.”

Why does the woman have pains during childbirth, and cramps and things like that? Because of sin. And Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. So in the kingdom, is she going to have menstrual cycles and cramps and all that? No. That’s going to be over. You women need to clap for that day.

This is some dark stuff right here. “Go thy way to a woman with child, and ask of her when she hath fulfilled her nine months, if her womb may keep the birth any longer within her.” So how long does a woman have to carry children now? Nine months. Hold that against 2 Esdras 6:21, where in the kingdom the women bring forth at three or four months.

I’m building something. “Consider thou therefore also, how that ye are less of stature than those that were before you. And so are they that come after you less than ye, as the creatures which now begin to be old, and have passed over the strength of youth.” The angel is telling Ezra that every generation we go weaker and weaker, smaller and smaller.

So remember this: because of sin she gets menstrual cycles, cramps, and sorrow in childbearing, and all of us get weaker and smaller. In the kingdom it is reversed, and we go to God level.

That’s one of my favorite scriptures in the Bible. “And in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name”. Seven is just a number of completion. Now put it with 2 Esdras 6:21 and Isaiah 60:22: the women bringing forth children every three or four months, and seven women to one man. That is how a little one shall become a thousand.

This is why Corinthians says we shall all be changed. “Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed”: that’s men and women. “In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.”

“For this corruptible must put on incorruption”: these little weak frail bodies we got, men and women, are going to put on incorruptible bodies. “And this mortal must put on immortality”: these mortal bodies that die from cancer and sickness and disease are going to be immortal. God level, baby. “Death is swallowed up in victory.”

I’m going to show you some God level stuff; we got a lot to rejoice about. “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days”: the sun shall be seven times brighter. “In the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound”: when the twelve tribes of Israel are gathered back together, we going to be on that God level, and everything is going to go back to the way it’s meant to be.

“And in that day will I make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven, and with the creeping things of the ground”: God is going to make a covenant, an agreement, with us and the animals. “And I will break the bow and the sword and the battle out of the earth”. Isaiah 11 shows what that covenant is.

“And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins. The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb”: this is the covenant. “And the leopard shall lie down with the kid”: everybody is going back to that vegan state. “And a little child shall lead them”: children are going to be able to lead these once vicious animals.

“And the cow and the bear shall feed; their young ones shall lie down together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox. And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice’ den.” That’s the covenant Hosea says God is going to make with us and the beasts of the field. Why? Because we are going to be immortal, on that celestial level, on that God level.

So it pleases us to stay in this truth; there is so much to rejoice and be honoured for. “But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.” The Lord prepared a whole lot for us.

“And the trumpet shall give a sound”: “For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air”.

“The men that are received shall see it, who have not tasted death from their birth”: that’s what Paul was talking about right there. “And the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain”: we which are alive, that’s Paul speaking, Paul included, “shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air”. So now we know what 2 Esdras 6:26 is talking about: that group of men that is going to be alive when the Lord returns.

What does it mean, the heart of the inhabitants shall “be changed, and turned into another meaning”? We just read it: “In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed. For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.” God level, men and women: celestial bodies, God bodies.

That’s what “the truth, which hath been so long without fruit” means. “Your houses will I give to a people that shall come; which not having heard of me yet shall believe me; to whom I have shewed no signs”: see that part there, no signs. We don’t see the signs like during the time of Moses, during the time of Elijah, during the time of Christ and the apostles. “Yet they shall do that I have commanded them.”

“They have seen no prophets”: we didn’t see Moses walking around, we don’t see Elijah, “yet they shall call their sins to remembrance, and acknowledge them.”

“For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind. But be ye glad and rejoice for ever in that which I create: for, behold, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy.” That new heaven and new earth is what we just read in 2 Esdras 6: Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.

“And the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voice of crying. There shall be no more thence an infant of days”: no more children dying in childbirth, “nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old”: that’s going to the other nations. “But the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed”: that’s the other nations; that ain’t talking about Israel.

“They shall not build, and another inhabit; they shall not plant, and another eat”: the curses of Deuteronomy 28:15 on will be finished. “For as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands. They shall not labour in vain, nor bring forth for trouble; for they are the seed of the blessed of the Lord, and their offspring with them.”

How many children? It said the women are going to bring forth children in three or four months. That’s about four children a year from one woman, and you got seven women to one man. There it is.

“And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear. The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent’s meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the Lord.”

sense.text: “To understand a proverb, and the interpretation; the words of the wise, and their dark sayings.”

“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.” So remember this, brothers and sisters: the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge. Make sure we walk the good walk and fight the good fight.
